items.title: Fix readMaterialDirtyFiles full-output trim in core/evidence-freshness.ts
items.context: readMaterialDirtyFiles (~line 153) does execFileSync('git',['status','--porcelain','--untracked-files=all']).trim() then line.slice(3): the first modified-tracked row's path loses its first character and isMaterialExcludedPath misfires, polluting materialDirty inside captureEvidenceHashSnapshot. Rework to the untrimmed raw-read pattern (see gitRaw in core/done-prepare-generated-metadata.ts:247) with per-line trimEnd.
items.userSees: ✓ evidence-freshness: first-row " M .lattice/…" row stays excluded from materialDirty; material path reported exactly

happy.desc: captureEvidenceHashSnapshot on a fixture whose first porcelain row is a modified-tracked .lattice metadata file reports dirty.files containing exactly the material path, with no corrupted lattice/... entry

edge.desc: clean tree yields empty dirty.files (emptiness decided on rows.length after per-line trimEnd, not raw-string truthiness)

adversarial.desc: scenario asserts porcelain row 0 matches /^ M / before any classification assertion, so the regression cannot pass vacuously if fixture ordering drifts

verificationEvidence.note: evidence-freshness first-row volatile row excluded, material path exact
evidence-freshness clean tree yields empty materialDirtyFiles
every scenario asserts porcelain row 0 is ' M .lattice/activity.jsonl' via assertFirstRowModifiedTracked before classification

items.title: Fix assertMaterialCleanForReview full-output trim in handlers/cross-host-review.ts
items.context: assertMaterialCleanForReview (~line 74) trims the full porcelain output then slice(3): a first-row ' M .lattice/...' metadata change parses as 'lattice/...' which fails the .lattice/ material-exclusion prefix and false-blocks the cross-host review dirty preflight. Same untrimmed raw-read fix.
items.userSees: ✓ cross-host-review: .lattice-only dirty tree passes the review preflight; a material row still refuses with the exact path

happy.desc: assertMaterialCleanForReview does NOT throw when the only dirty rows are .lattice metadata and the FIRST row is a modified-tracked .lattice file

adversarial.desc: a modified-tracked material row still throws and the error names the exact path (fail-closed behavior preserved, not loosened)

verificationEvidence.note: cross-host-review .lattice-only first-row dirt passes the preflight
cross-host-review clean tree passes the preflight
cross-host-review material row still refuses naming notes/keep.txt and no corrupted dot-less path

items.title: Fix gitPorcelainPaths and DONE-residue status trim in handlers/story-query.ts
items.context: gitPorcelainPaths (line 226) builds on gitOutput() which trims the full output, then slice(3): story_sync_main's dirty preflight (line 945) filters the corrupted first-row path through isVolatileRuntimeArtifactPath and can false-block sync with a corrupted path in the error. Also the DONE-residue probe (~line 1017) stores a full-trimmed status string whose first row is corrupted in display. Fix both reads to not trim leading output.
items.userSees: ✓ story-query: gitPorcelainPaths first entry keeps its leading dot; DONE-residue status text shows the untrimmed first row

happy.desc: gitPorcelainPaths returns the exact .lattice/... first-row path with its leading dot

edge.desc: rename rows (old -> new) still resolve to the new path after the raw-read conversion

adversarial.desc: a first-row volatile runtime-artifact path is correctly dropped by the story_sync_main isVolatileRuntimeArtifactPath filter (pre-fix code kept the corrupted path and false-blocked)

verificationEvidence.note: story-query first porcelain path keeps its leading dot
story-query rename rows resolve to the new path, no arrow strings leak
sync-main volatile filter drops the first-row volatile path leaving exactly the material path

items.title: Fix assertMainWorktreeClean input trim in core/partial-done-recovery.ts and brief rows in handlers/session.ts
items.context: partial-done-recovery.ts git() (line 23) trims full output; assertMainWorktreeClean (line 179) feeds it to materialStatusLines/statusLinePath (slice(3)) so a first-row volatile runtime artifact counts as material and done_recover falsely refuses. session.ts readGitStatus (line 150) trims full output before splitting rows for the session brief, so the first displayed row loses its status column. Fix both reads; keep bounded emptiness-only call sites unchanged.
items.userSees: ✓ partial-done-recovery: volatile-only first row no longer refuses done_recover; session brief rows keep their status columns

happy.desc: assertMainWorktreeClean does NOT throw when the only dirty row is a modified-tracked volatile runtime artifact on the FIRST porcelain row

edge.desc: session readGitStatus porcelain[0] matches /^ M / (status column preserved in brief rows)

adversarial.desc: a material modified-tracked row still makes assertMainWorktreeClean throw naming the exact path (refusal not loosened)

verificationEvidence.note: partial-done-recovery volatile-only first-row dirt does not refuse

items.title: Add first-row modified-tracked regression smoke and record the per-site audit verdict
items.context: New smoke task exercising the fixed consumers against a temp git repo whose FIRST porcelain row is a modified tracked file (' M' row, e.g. a .lattice/ or volatile path) plus a material row: assert exact path classification (pattern: assertModifiedTrackedPathExactness in tasks/done-prepare-merge-rerun-smoke.ts). Record the audit table (every porcelain call site -> fixed / safe-by-read-pattern / safe-by-usage / immune-by-format) in plan.md so untouched sites are auditable.
items.userSees: porcelain-first-row-audit-smoke: ALL PASS; run-all-smokes suite green

happy.desc: the new smoke passes against the fixed code, covering all four fixed consumers plus the session brief rows

edge.desc: the smoke is discovered by run-all-smokes via the dist/tasks/*-smoke.js convention and the full suite stays green

adversarial.desc: the smoke run against the pre-fix code FAILS (RED recorded before the fixes as repro evidence), proving the assertions detect the bug class
